analysis.evidence: Melchizedek speaks the blessing aloud. וַיֹּאמַר introduces his words, בָּרוּךְ אַבְרָם (“Blessed be Abram”), which name the recipient.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Piel wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular. The third person masculine singular object suffix הוּ refers to Abram.
analysis.sense: to speak a blessing upon another person

analysis.evidence: After וַיְבָרְכֵהוּ (“he blessed him”), וַיֹּאמַר introduces the words of the blessing, בָּרוּךְ אַבְרָם (“Blessed is Abram”).
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ marks a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular.

analysis.evidence: וַיְבָרְכֵהוּ וַיֹּאמַר introduces Melchizedek’s words of blessing. In בָּרוּךְ אַבְרָם לְאֵל עֶלְיוֹן, he pronounces Abram blessed by God Most High.
analysis.morphology: Qal passive participle, masculine singular absolute, agreeing with אַבְרָם and serving as its predicate.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: In בָּרוּךְ אַבְרָם, “blessed is Abram,” the name identifies the man whom Melchizedek blesses.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: In בָּרוּךְ אַבְרָם לְאֵל עֶלְיוֹן, Abram is blessed by God Most High. The following phrase קֹנֵה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ further identifies the God who blesses him.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ marks the source of the blessing. אֵל is a masculine singular absolute noun modified by עֶלְיוֹן.

analysis.evidence: In לְאֵל עֶלְיוֹן, “God Most High,” עֶלְיוֹן agrees with אֵל and serves as a divine epithet. The following phrase קֹנֵה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ describes the same God as maker of heaven and earth.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective modifying אֵל, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: קֹנֵה describes אֵל עֶלְיוֹן, “God Most High.” The coordinated nouns שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ complete the title, identifying heaven and earth as the whole of what God made and owns.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular construct, used as a title for God Most High.
